newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN says 115,000 Rwandan refugees flee Zaire camp.
newsitem.headline: UN says 115,000 Rwandan refugees flee Zaire camp.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency said on Thursday that some 115,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees had fled their camp of Kahindo in eastern Zaire's Goma region after overnight fighting and were heading south towards Goma town.
Spokeswoman Ruth Marshall told Reuters in Geneva: "Refugees started fleeing after two o'clock in the morning. As of mid-morning today (Thursday), the camp of Kahindo was empty."

Marshall said the refugees, joined by some 20,000 local Zairean villagers, were heading towards the sprawling Mugunga camp just outside Goma town which is already packed with 400,000 Hutus including some 200,000 who fled another camp in the region, Kibumba, after attacks last weekend.
Earlier on Thursday, heavy fighting between Tutsi guerrillas and Zairean troops rocked Goma town itself and a U.N. refugee agency spokesman in the town said that the airport had fallen.
Marshall said 14 UNHCR expatriate employees and another 86 staff members of Western aid agencies were trapped in Goma, which is already cut off from all aid routes.
